statements.text: To bolster this lie, they posted photographs that were generated by artificial intelligence programs.
statements.context: Senator Merkley's opening statement at a Congressional-Executive Commission on China hearing on transnational repression.

statements.text: Algorithms play a significant role in the way society interacts and behaves every single day, whether we like it or not. Because we know AI has the potential to exacerbate discrimination and inequality, federal agencies that employ the use of AI must have safeguards and boundaries in place to combat discrimination and bias.
statements.venue: Press release on Eliminating BIAS in Algorithmic Systems Act

statements.text: S. 4714. A bill to prohibit the distribution of false AI- generated election media and to amend the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 to prohibit the removal of names from voting rolls using unverified voter challenge databases; to the Committee on Rules and Administration.
statements.context: Senate floor introduction of bills and joint resolutions, with Senator Merkley introducing S. 4714 among a batch of unrelated bills.

statements.text: But buried nearly 300 pages into this bill is something quite shocking: a blanket, 10-year ban on States and local governments from regulating artificial intelligence.
statements.context: Senate floor speech during an executive session on the AI Civil Rights Act, opposing a 10-year state AI regulation moratorium included in a House reconciliation package.

statements.text: That is why I authored the AI Civil Rights Act, the most comprehensive AI legislation introduced in the U.S. Congress, which ensures that artificial intelligence serves the public good, not private profit exclusively. The bill would ensure that the AI age does not supercharge the bias and discrimination already prevalent today.

We want to reap the benefits of AI. We want to have AI be used across our society, but we also want to protect against the harmful effects of AI if it is put in the wrong hands to be used for the wrong purposes.

The UAE wanted advanced AI chips in order to have an advanced AI center in the United Arab Emirates. [...] Then a company closely associated with the UAE buys $2 billion of Trump's USD1 stablecoin. And then President Trump says: Oh, do you know what? You can have these AI chips after all. We will help you establish an advanced AI processing—artificial intelligence—center in Abu Dhabi, one of the UAE Emirates. That is corruption laid out as black and white as you could ever see it.
statements.context: Senate floor speech during motion to discharge on S.J. Res. 54, concerning cryptocurrency regulation and corruption allegations.

statements.text: Meanwhile, there was a desire by the foreign government to get access to highly capable AI chips. The answer was, no, we are not doing that. But then after they bought all these coins and enriched the President of the United States, well, then the President said: Let's give them the coins; let's give them these advanced chips.
statements.context: Senator Merkley is speaking on the Senate floor, alleging financial corruption by the President, including the claim that AI chip export controls were reversed after a foreign government purchased Trump-family stablecoins.

statements.text: The ballot box is the beating heart of democracy, and we must use every tool at our disposal to protect it. In the face of bad actors abusing AI to spread disinformation about voting to further dangerous voter suppression efforts, the FAIR Elections Act will help take on this 21st-century threat and stand up to the Trump Administration’s anti-democratic efforts to target eligible voters they don’t like.
statements.venue: Senate press release on FAIR Elections Act

statements.text: Bad actors are already using AI to file mass, baseless challenges against voters' registrations, scraping public data to manufacture doubt about who's eligible to vote.

"You need the equivalent of FDA controlling new drugs," Senator Merkley said Wednesday. "In this case, you're really talking about having an agency that's dedicated to making sure any new models coming out that are available are safe to use. And we don't really all understand what that means. Even the experts don't know what that means. This is all changing so fast in just a few years."
